correctness.rationale: The basis-pair Rota–Baxter identity for e1∘e1=2e2 yields four equations 2b²=0,2b(a−d)=0,2a(a−2d)=0,4ab=0. In odd characteristic b=0 and a(a−2d)=0; two affine planes intersect in q points, giving 2q²−q matrices and ranks 1,q²−1,q(q−1). The square ideal forces Aut=[[s,0],[t,s²]], and explicit conjugation acts transitively on c at each nonzero d, yielding 1 singleton, 1 orbit of q−1 and 2(q−1) orbits of q (total 2q). In characteristic two the product vanishes identically, all q^4 matrices qualify, their similarity class count is q²+q, and the ordinary 2×2 rank formulas hold. Substituting q^m in point polynomials gives the stated zeta functions. Independent direct basis-pair checks reproduced operator and rank counts for q=2,3,5,7: (16;1,9,6), (15;1,8,6), (45;1,24,20), (91;1,48,42); no finite test is used for universal proof.
